patients.summary: Construction laborer and heavy smoker who joined in 2019 healthy; ADPKD is found in 2022, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema in 2023 and Buerger disease in 2024, and an H. pylori gastric ulcer bleeds in 2026 and heals. He keeps smoking throughout.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31M establishing care. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

No active complaints. Physically demanding job (construction laborer, mostly site prep and framing crews). Back and shoulders ache by end of week, takes OTC ibuprofen 400-600 mg when it's bad, maybe a couple of times a week.

PMH: none he knows of. PSH: tonsils out at 8. Meds: OTC ibuprofen prn only. Allergies: none to medicines.
FH: father has polycystic kidney disease and is on dialysis. Mother has emphysema/COPD, quit smoking years ago. One older brother, healthy as far as he knows.
SH: single, lives in Amherst. Cigarettes since about 19, 1 to 1.5 ppd depending on the week. No alcohol at all. No drugs.

ROS: negative in detail - no chest pain, no dyspnea, no cough beyond a morning clear-throat, no GI or GU complaints, no headaches.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing, muscular. HEENT normal, tonsils absent. Neck supple, no nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, good air movement. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses felt. Ext warm, pulses 2+ radial and pedal. Skin: no rashes. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. Tobacco use, ~1-1.5 ppd x 12 yrs. Talked about quitting; he's not there yet ("maybe when the season slows down"). Offered patch/varenicline whenever he wants to try. Revisit each visit.
2. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids today. One-time HIV and hep C screens. Tdap (last one he remembers was high school) and flu shot given. PHQ-2 0.
3. Muscle aches from work: OTC ibuprofen ok occasionally, with food.
4. Father's kidney disease: noted. Will keep an eye on his own BP and creatinine.

RTC 1 year for physical, sooner prn. Text line explained.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Nathan - all of your labs came back fine. Kidney and liver tests, blood counts and cholesterol are in normal range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do except keep thinking about the cigarettes. Talk soon.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34M with headaches and palpitations.

HPI: Headaches since roughly last November - dull, both temples or band-like, come on in the afternoon, a few times a week, ibuprofen takes the edge off. No aura, no vision change, no weakness or numbness, not waking him from sleep. Separately, brief fluttering in the chest at rest, seconds at a time, a few times a week. No syncope, no chest pain with exertion. Asked about breathing: admits he gets winded hauling material up stairs on site more than he used to, "like I'm older than I am." No wheeze he's noticed. No fever, no weight change. Caffeine: two large coffees a day.

Meds: OTC ibuprofen prn. NKDA. Smoking 1-1.5 ppd.

Exam: BP 155/95 (rechecked after 5 min, same). HR and SpO2 as charted. Well appearing. Fundi grossly normal, no papilledema. Neck no bruit, thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abdomen: fullness in both flanks - large, smooth, nontender masses palpable bilaterally, ballotable. Soft bruit over the LUQ. No hepatomegaly. Ext no edema, pulses present. Neuro nonfocal.

ECG: sinus, normal.

A/P
1. Bilateral flank masses with elevated BP and a father with polycystic kidneys - this is polycystic kidney disease until proven otherwise. Renal ultrasound ordered. BMP, CBC.
2. BP 155/95 today. Headaches/palpitations could ride along with it. Adding TSH, aldosterone and renin to the draw. Recheck in two weeks with results.
3. Exertional breathlessness in a smoker: albuterol MDI prn for now, see if it helps. Lungs clear today.
4. Smoking - linked it to all three issues today. He listened. Still not ready.

RTC 2 wks.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt per PCP. Creatinine 1.2, upper end of normal. Aldosterone 21, a little above range; renin 3.4. Thyroid and blood count normal. PCP will go over at the 5/23 visit once the ultrasound is done. Ultrasound scheduled 5/17 at the imaging center, pt aware - drink water, full bladder not needed for this one. Pt verbalized understanding.

reports.text: Clinical history: bilateral flank masses. Technique: grayscale and color imaging of both kidneys and bladder. Right kidney measures 15.8 cm in length and left kidney 16.6 cm, both enlarged. Both kidneys contain multiple simple-appearing cysts of varying size throughout the cortex and medulla, replacing much of the normal parenchyma. No hydronephrosis. No shadowing stones. Bladder unremarkable. Liver normal in size and echotexture. Spleen normal in size.
reports.conclusion: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple bilateral renal cysts, compatible with polycystic kidney disease in the appropriate clinical setting. No hydronephrosis.

Follow-up, two weeks.

Still getting the headaches, maybe a little less. Palpitations a couple of times since last visit, brief. Albuterol: used it 3-4 times on site, thinks it helps some.

BP 155/95 again today, second visit in a row at that level. Exam unchanged - both flanks with large smooth masses, soft LUQ bruit, lungs clear, heart regular.

Data: ultrasound 5/17 - both kidneys enlarged (15.8 and 16.6 cm) and full of cysts, no hydronephrosis, liver normal. Creatinine 1.2. Aldosterone mildly high at 21 with renin 3.4. TSH normal.

A/P
1. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. Father has the same disease with kidney failure. Explained it's inherited, usually progresses slowly, and that BP control and kidney monitoring matter most. He was quiet, said he'd always figured it might be coming. Nephrology referral placed. The mildly high aldosterone fits the cystic kidneys rather than an adrenal problem.
2. BP 155/95 on two occasions. Before labeling hypertension I want home numbers - he'll buy a cuff and log twice daily for 2 weeks and send it in.
3. Headaches / palpitations: no red flags. Watch alongside BP. Less coffee.
4. Ibuprofen: with the kidneys, would rather he use as little as possible. Nephrology will weigh in.
5. Smoking: discussed again.

Portal the log; RTC after nephrology.

documents.title: Nephrology consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/20/2022
Reason: new diagnosis of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease

Thank you for referring this 34-year-old construction worker. Ultrasound in May showed bilaterally enlarged kidneys (15.8 and 16.6 cm) with numerous cysts. His father has ADPKD and is on dialysis. With that family history and the imaging, the diagnosis is secure; genetic testing is not needed for diagnosis.

Creatinine 1.2 in May. He brought a home BP log averaging in the mid-120s over 80. Office BP here 124/80. No gross hematuria, no flank pain episodes, no urinary infections.

Medications: albuterol inhaler as needed; over-the-counter ibuprofen. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: smokes 1-1.5 packs per day, no alcohol.

Exam: palpable kidneys bilaterally, nontender. Lungs clear. No edema.

Impression: ADPKD with preserved kidney function and normal home blood pressure.
Recommendations:
1. No antihypertensive at this time; continue home monitoring, target under 130/80.
2. Please avoid NSAIDs including ibuprofen; acetaminophen is the safer choice for aches.
3. Generous water intake through the day, moderate salt.
4. Kidney function and urine albumin yearly - happy for these to be drawn with you.
5. Strongly encourage stopping smoking.
6. I will see him yearly.

NKDA.
Nephrology

orders.reason: Progressive exertional dyspnea; brother with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
35M, breathing.

The winded feeling on site has been building for about a year. Now it's every flight of stairs with a load, and he stops halfway up a ladder run that he used to do without thinking. Albuterol helps a little, using it most workdays. No fevers, no blood in sputum, no chest pain, no ankle swelling. Usual smoker's morning cough.

The real reason he called: his older brother, 37, was just diagnosed with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency after a lung workup. Their mother has emphysema too. He's worried this is the same thing.

Smoking: still about a pack a day, "down from a pack and a half some weeks."

Exam: SpO2 95% at rest. No distress. Lungs: air movement reduced at the bases, no wheeze or crackles. Heart regular. No clubbing, no edema.

A/P
Progressive exertional dyspnea in a 35 y/o smoker with a brother newly diagnosed with AATD and a mother with emphysema. Needs a proper workup - pulmonology referral placed (they'll do imaging, PFTs and the AAT level/phenotype together). Continue albuterol prn. Asked him again to stop smoking; for the first time he said he'd "think hard about it." Gave quitline info and offered varenicline - wants to wait for the lung doctor's verdict.

events.reason: Progressive dyspnea; family history of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

reports.text: Technique: noncontrast CT of the chest, thin-section reconstructions. Lungs: diffuse emphysema, predominantly in the lower lobes, with a panlobular pattern and relative sparing of the upper lobes. No consolidation, nodule or mass. No pleural effusion. Airways patent. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen: both kidneys incompletely imaged, containing cysts, consistent with known polycystic kidney disease.
Acceptable and reproducible efforts. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62. FEV1 71% of predicted. FVC within normal limits. Minimal bronchodilator response.

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE - OUTSIDE CONSULT LETTER
Visit date: 05/30/2023
Referred by: primary care

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Webster for shortness of breath that has gradually worsened over the past year. His 37-year-old brother was recently found to have lung disease from alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency; his mother has emphysema. He smokes about a pack a day and has since his late teens. He works construction. Medications: albuterol as needed, occasional ibuprofen. NKDA.

On examination breath sounds were reduced on both sides and the bases were hyperresonant to percussion. No wheeze, no clubbing.

CT chest today shows diffuse emphysema that is worst at the bases. Spirometry: post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62, FEV1 71% predicted. Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin returned at 28 mg/dL, and phenotyping shows Pi*ZZ.

Impression: severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (ZZ) with basilar panlobular emphysema and moderate airflow obstruction, in an active smoker.

Plan
1. Smoking cessation is the single most important thing he can do. We talked frankly about how fast lungs decline in ZZ smokers. Nicotine replacement or varenicline are reasonable through your office.
2. Augmentation therapy (weekly IV alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor) was discussed. We do not start it while he is smoking; we will revisit once he has quit.
3. Continue albuterol as needed for now.
4. Keep vaccines current (influenza, COVID, pneumococcal - I see PCV20 was given last fall).
5. ZZ also affects the liver: a hepatic panel yearly would be appreciated, through your office.
6. Avoid dusty work without a respirator where he can.
7. Follow-up here in one year with repeat spirometry.

Allergies: NKDA.
Pulmonology

A/P

2. Tobacco - as above, revisit monthly by text if he's willing. He said yes.
3. ADPKD - nephrology in September.

orders.reason: Digital ulcers and extremity claudication in a heavy smoker

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
36M with ADPKD, AATD/emphysema, heavy smoker. Here for hand and foot symptoms.

HPI: About five months of fingers blanching white then dusky blue in the cold. Over the last couple of months, painful sores at several fingertips and a couple of toe tips that won't heal. Hands and feet ache after walking around the site, settles with rest. No joint pain or swelling, no rash, no fever, no weight loss, no dry eyes or mouth, no heartburn or trouble swallowing. Smoking about 1.5 ppd - went back up over the winter.

Meds: albuterol prn. Ibuprofen occasionally for the finger pain. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Shallow, punched-out ulcers at the tips of several fingers on both hands and two toes; no infection, no drainage. Fingers cool. Skin over fingers not thickened. Radial pulses present but weak; dorsalis pedis faint bilaterally. Cap refill sluggish. No joint synovitis.

A/P
Digital ischemic ulcers with cold-induced color change and limb claudication in a 36 y/o heavy smoker without diabetes or high cholesterol - thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger) is the leading concern. Checking A1c, lipids, ESR, CRP and ANA to look for other causes. Urgent vascular surgery referral.
Ulcer care: wash daily, petrolatum and a dry dressing, gloves and warm socks. Return or text for redness, spreading, or any dark/black skin.
Smoking: told him plainly that if this is Buerger, stopping completely is what saves the fingers and toes - even a few cigarettes keep it going. He was shaken. Nicotine patches/gum are not a good choice here; varenicline is. He wants to talk to the surgeon first.
Acetaminophen better than ibuprofen for the pain.

documents.title: Test results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Results: no diabetes (A1c 5.3), cholesterol normal, inflammation markers normal and the autoimmune screen (ANA) negative. That makes the smoking-related artery problem we talked about more likely. Vascular surgery has you on May 20 - the soonest they had. If any sore turns black, or a finger goes cold and won't warm up, call that day.

documents.title: Vascular surgery consultation
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/20/2024
Referring: primary care

HPI: 36-year-old man referred by his primary care physician (who also follows his ADPKD and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema, the latter managed by pulmonology). For roughly six months he has had pain in both hands and both feet that comes on with walking and eases at rest, painful sores at several fingertips, and fingers that turn white and then blue in cold weather. No fever, no joint pains, no weight loss.

PMH: ADPKD (normal kidney function, followed by nephrology); alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema. No diabetes, hypertension or hyperlipidemia.
PSH: tonsillectomy in childhood.
Meds: albuterol inhaler prn; ibuprofen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father ADPKD with ESRD; mother emphysema/COPD (ex-smoker); older brother AATD.
SH: cigarettes 1.5 packs/day for 15 years, 22.5 pack-years. No alcohol. Construction laborer.

Vitals: T 36.8 C (98.2 F), BP 124/78, HR 76, RR 14.
Exam: shallow ulcerations at the tips of several fingers and several toes, bilaterally. No joint swelling or erythema. Radial and dorsalis pedis pulses diminished on both sides. Capillary refill delayed in fingers and toes. Remainder of the exam unremarkable.

PCP labs April 2024: A1c 5.3, lipids normal, ESR/CRP normal, ANA negative.

Impression: thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger disease) - young heavy smoker, distal upper and lower limb ischemia with digital ulceration, no atherosclerotic risk factors, autoimmune screen negative.

Plan:
1. Complete abstinence from all tobacco and nicotine products. This is the treatment. Without it, progression and amputation risk are high. Discussed in detail; varenicline through PCP would be appropriate, not nicotine replacement.
2. Local wound care: daily cleansing, nonadherent dressing; protect from cold and trauma.
3. Arteriography of the hands and feet to confirm the pattern; scheduled.
4. Follow-up one year, sooner for any nonhealing or worsening ulcer.

NKDA.
Vascular Surgery

documents.title: Vascular surgery letter - arteriogram
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY - INTERVAL LETTER
Re: arteriography 06/06/2024

Upper and lower extremity arteriography was performed via right common femoral access without complication.
Findings: proximal arteries of both arms and legs are smooth with no atherosclerotic plaque and no source of emboli. There are segmental occlusions of the digital arteries of both hands and of the distal tibial arteries of both legs, with corkscrew collateral vessels around the occlusions.
Conclusion: findings typical of thromboangiitis obliterans. No lesion suitable for revascularization.

Plan unchanged: total tobacco abstinence, wound care, follow-up in a year.
NKDA.
Vascular Surgery

documents.title: Vascular surgery follow-up
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 05/29/2025

37-year-old with thromboangiitis obliterans (diagnosed here 05/2024, arteriogram 06/2024), alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and ADPKD, back about a year after his first visit. His symptoms have moved on: the hand and foot pain that used to come with walking is now there at rest, worst at night. In cold, the fingers go pale, then blue, then red and throbbing as they warm. Within the last month he has developed painful sores at the tips of two fingers and one toe. Denies fever, weight loss and joint pains.

Meds: albuterol prn; ibuprofen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: 15 years of smoking; now about 1 pack per day. No alcohol, no drugs.

Exam: small shallow ulcers at the right fingertips and at the tip of the left great toe, clean bases. Hair growth diminished over both lower legs. Dorsalis pedis pulses mildly decreased bilaterally. Radial and ulnar pulses palpable. Digital Allen test abnormal in both hands.

Impression: Buerger disease, progressing to rest pain with new digital ulceration, in the setting of ongoing smoking.

Plan:
1. Smoking cessation once more - the only thing shown to halt this. He was told that continued smoking is likely to lead to digit loss.
2. Wound care as before; protect from cold.
3. No revascularization option per prior arteriogram.
4. Return in one year, sooner for nonhealing ulcer, color change to black, or infection.

NKDA.
Vascular Surgery

Text photos every 2 weeks until healed.

documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE - OUTSIDE HOSPITAL
Date of service: 05/18/2026

CC: upper abdominal pain, black stools

HPI: 38 y/o M with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, ADPKD and Buerger disease. Burning pain in the upper abdomen for about 2 months. Comes on a few hours after he eats, eases for a while if he eats again or takes an antacid. For the last week his stools have been dark. No vomiting, no hematemesis, no lightheadedness or syncope. Takes ibuprofen on and off for muscle and night pain.

PMH: AATD with emphysema, ADPKD, Buerger disease, tobacco use.
PSH: tonsillectomy as a child.
Home meds: albuterol inhaler prn. Ibuprofen OTC occasionally.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father ADPKD with ESRD; mother emphysema/COPD; older brother AATD.
SH: 1 pack per day cigarettes. No alcohol.

Vitals: within normal limits throughout, see flowsheet.
Exam: alert, comfortable. Abdomen soft with mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding or rebound. Rectal: dark brown stool, guaiac positive. Lungs diminished at bases. Healing fingertip and toe ulcers.

Labs: CBC normal, hemoglobin within range. BMP unremarkable apart from creatinine just above range, in keeping with his known polycystic kidney disease.

Course: Hemodynamically stable. GI consulted and performed upper endoscopy this afternoon (see GI report): 1.2 cm lesser-curvature gastric ulcer, biopsied. Observed overnight; tolerated diet, no further bleeding, hemoglobin stable on repeat. Discharged 05/19 in the morning.

Diagnosis: gastric ulcer with bleeding.
Discharge plan: omeprazole 40 mg twice daily. Stop ibuprofen and all NSAIDs. Biopsy results to PCP and GI. See PCP within 1 week. Return for vomiting blood, fainting, or black stools that worsen.

documents.title: Upper endoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ESOPHAGOGASTRODUODENOSCOPY - OUTSIDE HOSPITAL GI
Date: 05/18/2026
Indication: epigastric pain, melena, guaiac-positive stool; NSAID use.
Sedation: moderate, monitored. Tolerated well.

Findings:
- Esophagus: normal.
- Stomach: a single 1.2 cm clean-based ulcer along the lesser curvature of the gastric body, no visible vessel, no active bleeding. Surrounding mucosa mildly erythematous. Biopsies taken from the ulcer edge and from antrum and body for H. pylori.
- Duodenum: normal to the second portion.

Impression: gastric ulcer, lesser curvature, 1.2 cm, no stigmata of recent hemorrhage requiring treatment.
Recommendations: PPI twice daily; avoid NSAIDs; follow biopsies; treat H. pylori if present; repeat EGD in 8-12 weeks to document healing.
NKDA.
Gastroenterology

reports.text:
Specimens: A. gastric ulcer edge, biopsy. B. gastric antrum and body, biopsies.
Microscopic: A. Ulcer edge with granulation tissue and fibrinopurulent debris; adjacent mucosa with chronic active gastritis. B. Chronic active gastritis with numerous curved rod-shaped organisms on the surface epithelium, confirmed by immunostain as Helicobacter pylori. No intestinal metaplasia. No dysplasia. No malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Gastric ulcer edge and gastric mucosa with Helicobacter pylori-associated chronic active gastritis. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

events.reason: Repeat upper endoscopy for gastric ulcer healing
